newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend record march on election calm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend record march on election calm.

text.p: Mexican shares continued their advance into record territory at midday Monday as local buyers stepped in who had previously stood on the sidelines before Sunday's elections, traders and analyst said.

"Brokers who had stayed away because they forecast post-electoral conflict are the ones who are buying now. Institutional investors are standing firm," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index was up 60.34 points, or 1.30 percent, to a trading record of 4,704.94.
Trading volume of 65.9 million shares was moderate compared to many recent sessions due to the relative lack of foreign players in the market, dealers said.
"Locals are buying, the ones who were cautious before the elections, but volume is a little thin as there are few foreign dealers in the market," a desk trader said.
Dealers and investment strategists on Wall Street told Reuters they were wary of profit-taking following the bourse's sharp, virtually uninterrupted rise in recent weeks.

"The PRI's (ruling party's) loss of Congress comes as a minor surprise, which I don't think all investors have priced in yet," said Geoffrey Dennis, an investment strategist at HSBC-James Capel in New York.
"There is the possibility of a correction, but dealers would then use this as a buying opportunity," he added.

Mexico voted on Sunday for to renew the lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time in modern history, a mayor of Mexico City. The post had been previously occupied by a presidential nominee.

Returns from 85 percent of polling booths counted nationwide showed President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) had lost overall control of the lower house for the first time since 1929.

A preliminary count showed Cuauhtmoc Crdenas of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) had beaten the PRI candidate in the race for Mexico City, the nerve centre of the highly centralized country.
Analysts stressed the relative lack of allegations of foul play that had often sullied elections in the past, were almost as important as the results themselves.
On the broad market, gainers had far outstripped sliders by 72 to 16 out of a total of 105 stocks traded.
